source.title: Different roles for amygdala central nucleus and substantia innominata in the surprise-induced enhancement of learning

confidence_rationale: Transient-inactivation dissociation: CeA is needed at the time of surprise, not when faster learning is later expressed; SI/nBM (cholinergic) is needed at expression, not at surprise. Supports MECH-598's separation of an event-time associability WRITE from a later-trial associability READ, i.e. a persistent state. Appetitive, omission-induced paradigm, so the aversive trigger is not tested.
failure_signatures: CeA inactivation at the time of surprise abolishes the later learning advantage, so a mechanism whose associability write happens at a different time from the PE event would not match this dissociation.

The expression side depends on cholinergic basal forebrain, i.e. a neuromodulatory gain at read-out time -- a claim that locates all of the effect in the per-cue state and none in a read-out gain overstates what the data show.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Surprise-induced enhancement of later learning about a stimulus requires intact CeA function when surprise occurs but not when the faster learning is expressed; SI/nBM function is required at expression but not at the time of surprise.
mapping.ree_translation: Maps onto MECH-598's two-stage structure: an aversive PE event WRITES raised associability onto candidates present, and a later encounter READS it as a faster learning rate. The dissociation argues these are separate operations with separate substrates, which is the difference between a persistent associability state and a one-shot boost (the claim's frozen-associability falsifier).
mapping.mapping_caveat: Appetitive food paradigm; surprise produced by omitting an expected event. The SI/nBM expression role is cholinergic, which puts part of the effect in a read-out gain, closer to MECH-398 (ACh plasticity gain) than to a pure per-cue state. REE's control arm is a matched broadcast gain; this paper suggests biology uses both.
mapping.source_context: Rat, serial-prediction task, transient pharmacological inactivation of CeA or SI/nBM at surprise vs test

confidence_components.notes: Clean four-experiment inactivation design, one lab. Mapping good for the encode/express structure, weak for the valence.
